user.description: Choose Configure KSM to set defaults for future devices, or enter a device address to add one. A device already running Kiosk Satellite is added over its own API; ADB is only needed to install it.

onboard_device_owner.title: Enable Device Owner for Kiosk Satellite
onboard_device_owner.description:
Device Owner gives Kiosk Satellite full control of this device.

**Benefits**
- Kiosk Satellite updates install silently, with no on-screen prompt.
- True kiosk lock: the app can pin itself so users cannot leave it.
- Kiosk Satellite can make itself the home app without a prompt.
- Remote reboot from Home Assistant.
- The real Wi-Fi MAC address is readable.

**Side effects**
- It cannot be undone except by a factory reset. Kiosk Satellite cannot be uninstalled normally while it is Device Owner.
- To enroll, the accounts below are removed from the device. Their app is removed for a moment and then reinstalled. On a Meta Portal this removes the Portal's Meta login: KSM then opens Meta's setup screen on the Portal, and you finish setup and sign in with Facebook or WhatsApp there, once. The Portal will not reboot or reset; the setup screen only looks like a first start.
- Some OEM features that need an account (for example Meta's calling and apps) may stop working until you sign in again.

**Accounts on this device**
{accounts}

Tick the box and submit to proceed. Nothing on the device changes until you do. Leave it unticked to skip Device Owner; the device is added either way.

data.confirm: I understand this cannot be undone without a factory reset

onboard_android9_cleanup.title: Clean and take ownership of this Android 9 Portal
onboard_android9_cleanup.description: This removes the Portal's Meta accounts and sign-in, clears Meta app data, disables audited Meta launcher and services, and makes Kiosk Satellite Device Owner. Device Owner requires a factory reset to undo. Native Kiosk Satellite Home must already be enabled and selected as Android Home. Network ADB is checked before and after cleanup, but whether it survives a reboot is not yet verified. Keep physical access to the Portal. Leave the box unticked to add the device without cleanup.

data.confirm: Erase Meta sign-in and clean this Android 9 Portal

device_password.title: Update Kiosk Satellite password
device_password.description: Enter this device's current Kiosk Satellite Web UI password. The stored password changes only after Kiosk Satellite accepts it.

device_host.title: Change how KSM reaches this device
device_host.description: Enter the new DNS name or IP address, without https:// or a port. KSM checks that Kiosk Satellite answers there with this device's saved key, and changes nothing if it does not. Use an IP address if the device's DNS name points at a reverse proxy: KSM must reach the device directly.

device_rename.title: Rename Kiosk Satellite device
device_rename.description: This changes the Kiosk Satellite name, hostname and ESPHome node, then updates the KSM entry. On a Meta Portal it also changes Android's Portal Name over one temporary ADB connection: enable network ADB on the Portal before submitting, then you can turn it off again. A DNS hostname changes only after the new name resolves to this device. Review the result for incomplete layers and old ESPHome action callers.

init.title: Configure Kiosk Satellite Manager
init.description: Install version and backup settings apply to every device now; the other settings apply to future devices only. Leave the password empty to retain it. A backup period of 0 turns automatic backups off.

data_description.target_version: Latest follows the newest release. A downloaded version becomes what every device installs, so an upgrade can be tested. Devices only move forward; Kiosk Satellite refuses downgrades.

meta_setup.title: Set up the Portal's Meta login again
meta_setup.description:
Kiosk Satellite is already Device Owner, but this Portal's Meta login is gone (Device Owner enrollment removes it). KSM can put Meta's setup screen back on the Portal: it turns kiosk mode off, resets Meta's setup app and opens it. You then finish setup and sign in with Facebook or WhatsApp on the Portal, and KSM turns kiosk mode back on once the Meta login is back.

Tick the box and submit to show the setup screen.

data.confirm: Show Meta's setup screen on the Portal

device_https_enable.title: Use HTTPS for this device
device_https_enable.description:
KSM will switch Kiosk Satellite's management port to HTTPS and pin the device's own self-signed key, so the device password and Home Assistant token never cross the network in plaintext.

After the switch the device's web page answers only at https://{host}:2324; http:// stops working. Your browser warns about the self-signed certificate the first time you open it there — that warning is expected.

Needs Kiosk Satellite 2026.9.78 or later.

device_https_disable.title: Switch this device back to HTTP
device_https_disable.description:
This device is managed over pinned HTTPS. KSM will turn Use HTTPS off in Kiosk Satellite, wait for it to answer at http://{host}:2324, and then drop the pinned key.

After that the device password and Home Assistant token travel in plaintext on your network.

data.confirm: Switch this device back to HTTP

confirm.title: Trust the new HTTPS key for {name}?
confirm.description:
Kiosk Satellite at {host} is presenting a different HTTPS key than the one Home Assistant pinned. This is expected after using "Replace certificate" in Kiosk Satellite or after a factory reset; otherwise someone may be intercepting the connection. Until you confirm, Home Assistant will not send the device any credentials or settings.

Submit to trust the key the device is presenting now.

abort.cannot_connect: The device did not answer over HTTPS. Check it is online and try again.
abort.entry_not_found: This device is no longer configured.

confirm.title: Manage {name} over HTTP?
confirm.description:
Kiosk Satellite at {host} now answers over plain HTTP, but Home Assistant has it pinned to HTTPS, so management is blocked. This happens when Use HTTPS is turned off in Kiosk Satellite. If nobody turned it off, something else may be answering at this address — do not confirm.

Submit to drop the pinned key and manage the device over HTTP; the device password and Home Assistant token then travel in plaintext. To keep HTTPS instead, turn Use HTTPS back on in Kiosk Satellite.

abort.cannot_connect: The device did not answer over HTTP. Check it is online and try again.
abort.entry_not_found: This device is no longer configured.

confirm.title: Add {name} to Kiosk Satellite Manager?
confirm.description:
{name} at {host} joined {leader}'s fleet, and Kiosk Satellite Manager does not manage it.

Submit to show it under Discovered, where you enter its Kiosk Satellite password. Ignore this repair to leave it unmanaged; it will not be raised again.

dashboard_dns_mismatch.title: {name}: dashboard address resolves differently
dashboard_dns_mismatch.description:
{name} ({host}) resolves {hostname} to {device_address}, but Home Assistant resolves it to {ha_addresses}. Kiosk Satellite loads the dashboard from the device's answer, so it can reach the wrong server or refuse its HTTPS certificate and show a black screen.

Make the device use your local DNS: on Android, set Settings → Network → Private DNS to Off, or fix the DNS servers DHCP gives its network. Then press Install Kiosk Satellite to check again; this repair clears once both answers agree.

device_support.title: {name}: device not in Kiosk Satellite Manager's library

confirm.title: Request support for {name}?
confirm.description:
Kiosk Satellite Manager has no tested install recipe for {name}, so it will not install Kiosk Satellite on it. You can ask for it to be added to the device library.

Submit to read the device's identity over ADB: manufacturer, model, Android version, build fingerprint and similar read-only facts. Its address, name, accounts and credentials are not included. Nothing is sent until you open the link on the next step.

send.title: Send the support request for {device}
send.description:
Kiosk Satellite Manager prepared a request to add **{device}** to its library.

- Request: {kind}
- Proposed library entry: `{model_key}`
- Closest existing recipe: `{candidate}`

[Open the pre-filled GitHub issue]({url}), review it, and submit it there (a GitHub account is needed). If the report field is empty, attach this device's Download diagnostics.

Submit here once you have sent it; this repair will not come back for {name}.

abort.now_supported: Kiosk Satellite Manager now recognizes {name} and has a recipe for it. Press Install Kiosk Satellite on the device's page.
abort.cannot_connect_adb: Could not connect to {name} over ADB. Turn on network debugging (Developer options → ADB over network or Wireless debugging), accept the authorization prompt on the device, and try again.
abort.entry_not_found: This device is no longer configured.

factory_reset.title: {name}: Kiosk Satellite is the Device Owner

confirm.title: Open the factory reset screen on {name}?
confirm.description:
Kiosk Satellite is the Device Owner on {name}, so Android will not uninstall it. Only a factory reset removes it.

A factory reset erases everything on the device: Kiosk Satellite, every setting, and every account and sign-in. To use Kiosk Satellite on it again you will install it and set up Device Owner again.

Submit to turn off the kiosk lock and open the device's own factory reset screen. Nothing is erased until a person on the device presses Reset there; pressing Cancel leaves the device as it is, with the kiosk lock off until you turn it back on in Kiosk Satellite.

abort.factory_reset_failed: The factory reset screen did not open on {name}. The kiosk lock was turned back on. Open Settings on the device and reset it from there.
